SAIL Rating System

SAIL rating system

The most comprehensive system for evaluating sovereign AI strategies and systems.

Barcelona Supercomputing Centre | SAIL-certified AI infrastructure facility

SAIL-certified sovereign AI systems are better systems

SAIL (Sovereign AI Leadership) is a rating and evaluation system that provides a structured assessment of a country's or agency's AI sovereignty across technical, legal, and governance dimensions. It offers a point-based system that signals resilience, control, and strategic leadership.

SAIL serves as a globally recognized symbol of sovereignty leadership, supported by a committed community of governments, agencies, and technical partners driving market transformation toward resilient AI governance.

SAIL is designed for all AI governance contexts

SAIL applies to national strategies, ministries, agencies, and public programs that deploy or govern AI systems. Whether assessing sovereign capacity in applications, data, models, or infrastructure, SAIL helps governments identify strengths and dependencies, optimize capacity, and benchmark progress over time.

AI governance contexts - national, ministry, agency, program

How SAIL works

SAIL is holistic. As a framework, it evaluates sovereignty across seven layers—from applications and orchestration to compute and legal governance—through a series of credit categories tailored for each assessment track. To achieve SAIL certification, an entity must first satisfy baseline prerequisites and then accrue points by fulfilling credit criteria. Assessments are independently verified and award points that correspond to a level of SAIL certification: Certified, Silver, Gold, and Platinum.

Platinum
80+ points
Gold
60–79 points
Silver
50–59 points
Certified
40–49 points

SAIL Assessment Process

1

Select the appropriate SAIL track and scope

Determine whether the assessment applies to a national strategy, ministry, agency, or specific program, and review relevant prerequisites.

2

Register the assessment

Provide baseline documentation and define the scope of AI systems, governance processes, and dependencies.

3

Build the SAIL scorecard

Choose the credits aligned with your strategy and map responsibilities for evidence gathering and documentation.

4

Implement sovereignty strategies

Execute technical, organizational, and legal actions needed to meet prerequisites and pursue credit categories.

5

Submit for verification

Upload evidence to the SAIL review portal and undergo independent verification for scoring and certification.

Understanding SAIL and Getting Started

Before pursuing SAIL certification:

  • Review prerequisites – Ensure your entity meets the minimum requirements for certification (e.g., legal authority, inventory of AI use).
  • Select the relevant track – Choose the right assessment track depending on whether you are assessing national, subnational, or programmatic sovereignty.
  • Explore the credit library – Identify which credits are achievable and which require further capacity building.

Getting started guide - SAIL assessment flowchart

Certification and Recognition

Once certified, projects have joined a select group of leaders in AI. They can then order or download a certificate for display, and share the news through a coordinated press release.
